description: Renovate for the GitLab lane on gitlab.tomlawson.io (ai/orbit-launcher), taking over from the retired .github/dependabot.yml (#140 step 4). Same cadence and the same grouping the Dependabot file had, so nothing about what gets watched changes with the host.

GitHub Actions is watched from here too, matching the actions entry the retired .github/dependabot.yml carried, plus the .gitlab-ci.yml job images and the pipeline's own digest pins, which Dependabot never watched because .gitlab-ci.yml did not exist when it was written.

This file is read two ways: as the repository config Renovate finds on the repository's default branch, and as the global config the renovate job in .gitlab-ci.yml points RENOVATE_CONFIG_FILE at. On GitLab the default branch is `dev`, which carries this file, and the weekly schedule runs on `dev` too, so both readings resolve to this same copy and the repository one merges over the global one -- see the job's comment.

The dependency dashboard is off (owner, 2026-09-10). It is a bot-written issue with no acceptance criteria that never reaches a done state, so it cannot sit in a milestone that reports as finished, and it is stale between runs. Turning it off changes nothing about what Renovate watches or raises: the merge requests still arrive. ai/orbit turned it off on 2026-09-08 and ai/mikroview on 2026-09-10, for the same reason; this matches them.

npm is enabled only for test/visual/package.json's @playwright/test (#179): that is the only package.json in the repo, so this does not widen what gets watched beyond it. Before this, Renovate could move PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE without ever touching the lockfile, which is what #161 found broken; test/supplychain/pins_test.go now also checks the two agree.

customManagers.description: The pipeline pins its job images in the top-level variables block -- GO_IMAGE, PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE, UBUNTU_IMAGE -- and the jobs reference them as $GO_IMAGE, $PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE and $UBUNTU_IMAGE. The gitlabci manager reads image: and services: keys, so it sees the variable references and never the pins themselves. This reads the pins directly.

GO_VERSION's own value (#179), read so it can be grouped with GO_IMAGE below even though .gitlab-ci.yml names the same release two different ways -- a Docker tag for the image, a bare version here. The golang-version datasource tracks the same upstream releases as the image's golang repository, so the two stay comparable.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes do not wait for Monday. GitLab CE has no dependency-alert API for Renovate to read, so osvVulnerabilityAlerts above is what supplies the advisories, from the OSV database, and this is what lets a fix land outside the weekly window.

packageRules.description: Go modules: the go-minor-patch group the Dependabot file had. Majors are left out of the group so a breaking change is reviewed on its own.
GitHub Actions: the actions-minor-patch group the Dependabot file had. Majors separate, as everywhere else here.

The pipeline's own images -- GO_IMAGE, PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE and UBUNTU_IMAGE from the custom manager above, and anything the gitlabci manager finds in a literal image: key (the renovate job's own image below). Dependabot never watched any of this -- .gitlab-ci.yml did not exist when it was written -- so this is new cover rather than a like-for-like replacement.

PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE and @playwright/test must move together or the gate breaks the way #161 found it: the image is chosen so no browser download happens in the `visual` job, which only holds while the image and the lockfile name the same Playwright release. test/supplychain/pins_test.go (#179) now checks the two agree; this makes Renovate propose them as one merge request instead of two. Listed after the image group above so this grouping wins for these two packages.

GO_IMAGE and GO_VERSION must move together or staticcheck breaks on the newer toolchain's export data, the way #161 found it. GO_SHA256 and STATICCHECK_VERSION cannot be derived by Renovate -- a checksum and a separate project's release -- so test/supplychain/pins_test.go (#179) checks those by hand and names them in its failure message. Listed after the image group above so this grouping wins for these two packages.

Renovate's own image, which the gitlabci manager finds in the renovate job. 44.63.0 and 44.64.0 (both released 2026-09-04) do not start: they ship an `apk` datasource that imports `tar`, and `tar` is absent from the image's node_modules, so the container dies before it reads any configuration. Only those two are excluded, so the next working release is offered as usual. Nothing runs this job outside the weekly schedule, so a bump is only proven by the next scheduled run: if that run fails at start-up, revert the bump and add the version here.
